title: Appliance and safety checks
audience: Short-stay turnover cleaners who check appliances and safety items during a turnover.
learningOutcomes: Check the visible state of appliances and safety items without operating unfamiliar appliances.
Identify faults, damage and missing safety items, and report them.
Keep the appliance and its power and gas connections undisturbed.

instruction.heading: Visible checks only
instruction.body: Your check is a visual one. Look at each appliance and its connections as they sit in the room. Check the cord for fraying, cuts, kinks, exposed wire, or a cord that has been taped or joined. Check the plug for scorching, discolouration, a loose fit or a cracked casing, and check the power point it is in for scorch marks, a loose cover or a plate that sits unevenly. Check the appliance housing for heat marks, leaks, or damaged controls. Check smoke alarms and fire blankets where the property has them, for obvious damage, a missing item, or a visible expiry date that has passed. Do not switch on an unfamiliar electrical or gas appliance to show that it works. Do not open its panels, take off its covers, or unplug it, and do not move a heater or a cooktop to see behind it. If the property procedure permits a test of a smoke alarm, follow that procedure and no other.

instruction.heading: Reporting faults at once
instruction.body: Report any fault, damaged cord, scorch mark, loose plug or missing safety item to the coordinator straight away, before you move on to other tasks. Mark the appliance as not to be used, using the tag or sign the property procedure provides, and leave it unused until a qualified person has checked it. Do not repair a cord by taping it, and do not replace a plug, a socket or a fitting. A gas smell is an emergency, and it is handled differently from other faults. Leave the immediate area, keep others away, and follow the gas steps in the safety section. Do not search for the source of a gas smell yourself, and do not use a flame, a switch or an appliance while you are in the area.

instruction.heading: Recording each check
instruction.body: Record each check and each fault with the appliance, its location, the time, and what you saw. Use the word checked, not working, unless the check was authorised and included a function test by a person who is allowed to carry one out. Do not record an appliance as safe to use unless the procedure says that a visual check is enough to make that statement. Include a photograph where the property rules allow it, with the fault and a reference point in view. Record who you told and the time you told them. This lesson does not grant any electrical or gas licence, and a visual check is not an inspection or a certificate.

procedure: Check the visible state of each appliance, its cord, its plug and the power point it uses, from a distance that does not require moving the appliance.
Check smoke alarms and fire blankets for obvious damage, missing items or an expired date, and test a smoke alarm only if the property procedure permits it.
Do not operate an unfamiliar appliance, open its panels, unplug it, or move it.
Report any fault, scorch mark, damaged cord or missing safety item at once, and mark the appliance as not to be used.
For a gas smell, leave the immediate area, keep others away, avoid switches and flames, and follow the emergency steps.
Record each check and each fault with the appliance, location, time, photograph reference and the person told.

workedExamples.situation: During a turnover you notice a scorch mark on a power point and a cord that is frayed near the kettle.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you do with the kettle and the power point?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not use the kettle or the power point, and do not plug anything into the scorched point. Record the scorch mark and the frayed cord with their locations, the time and a photograph where permitted. Report both to the coordinator at once, and mark the kettle as not to be used. Leave both unused until a qualified person has checked them. Do not tape the cord, and do not replace the plug.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner enters a unit and notices a gas smell in the kitchen, with the cooktop switched on at the knob.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the first action, and what must you not do?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not switch anything on or off, including the lights, the extraction fan or the cooktop, and do not use a flame. If it is safe to do so and the procedure trains you to, turn off the gas supply at the meter or the cylinder. Otherwise leave the area, keep others away, and open windows and doors only if you can reach them without touching a switch. Call the emergency contact in the business procedure and the gas distributor from outside the property. If the smell continues, or there is a fire, call 000 and evacuate. Record the time and what you saw. Do not search for the leak yourself.

workedExamples.situation: A smoke alarm in a hallway is missing from its ceiling bracket, and a fire blanket in the kitchen has an expired date.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Do you replace the alarm or the blanket, and what do you record?
workedExamples.reasoning: No. Replacing or installing a safety item is outside the cleaner's role unless the procedure gives the task. Record the missing alarm and the expired blanket with their locations and the time, and report both to the coordinator at once. Do not test the remaining alarms unless the procedure permits it. Leave the blanket where it is and mark it for replacement.

equipmentAndPpe: Visible-check checklist for appliances, cords, plugs, power points and safety items.
Do-not-use tag or sign, as the property procedure provides.
Fault report form, with fields for location, description, time and the person told.
Torch for a visual check of a dark area, used to look only and not to probe, touch or open anything.
Camera for permitted photographs of faults.
Emergency contact details from the business procedure, carried on the job sheet.

commonErrors.error: Using an appliance with a frayed cord to test it.
commonErrors.prevention: Do not use it. Mark it, and report it.

commonErrors.error: Taping a cord, or replacing a plug or a socket.
commonErrors.prevention: Report the cord or plug as faulty. The cleaner does not repair it.

commonErrors.error: Recording an appliance as working without a check that allowed it.
commonErrors.prevention: Record only what was checked, and use the word checked rather than working.

commonErrors.error: Searching for a gas leak yourself, or using a switch or a flame to look.
commonErrors.prevention: Leave the area and follow the emergency steps.

commonErrors.error: Moving or unplugging a hot appliance to see behind it.
commonErrors.prevention: Check from where you stand, and report what you cannot see.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Electrical work in New South Wales. The NSW Government page, last updated 23 June 2026, says that electrical wiring work, including repairing and altering an installation, needs a licence or certificate. It also says that plug-in electrical articles and some low-voltage equipment are outside the definition of an electrical installation. The page does not mention testing or using appliances.

Gas appliances. Queensland's gas safety guidance says that only a licensed gasfitter can do gas work, which includes installing, altering, repairing, servicing, testing or certifying a gas system, and that a gas smell which persists after the supply is shut off calls for 000. Victoria's emergency guidance says to stop ignition sources, avoid switches, open doors and windows where it is safe, keep people away, and contact the gas distributor, whose number is listed on the page and varies by area.
This lesson does not grant any electrical or gas licence, and a visual check is not a function test, an inspection or a certificate of safety.
The cleaner records what is seen and reports it.

qualityStandard: A visible check is completed for each appliance and safety item listed on the property checklist.
A simulated scorch mark and frayed cord are reported and marked as not to be used, and are not used in the case study.
The gas-smell response is demonstrated in the role-play: no switches, no flames, no search for the source, and the emergency steps followed.
Each record uses the word checked, and no appliance is recorded as safe without an authorised basis.
documentationEvidence: Appliance check record with appliance, location, time and what was seen.
Fault report for each defect found, with the do-not-use marking and the person told.
Photograph references for faults, where permitted.
summary: Check the visible state only, and do not operate unfamiliar appliances or open them.
Report faults and missing safety items at once, and mark the appliance as not to be used.
A gas smell means no switches or flames, no search for the leak, and the emergency steps.

knowledgeChecks.question: A cord is frayed. What is correct?
options: Use it carefully until the end of the stay
Do not use it, and report it at once
Tape the cord and use it for the job

knowledgeChecks.question: You smell gas during a turnover. What is correct?
options: Look for the source yourself with a lit match in the room and the hall
Open a window and carry on with the cleaning in the room and the hall today
Keep people away, avoid switches and flames, and follow the emergency steps

knowledgeChecks.question: Should you operate an unfamiliar appliance to show it works?
options: No, check the visible state only
Yes, to be sure it is safe
Yes, if the guest asks you to
